subject.title: fix(agents): keep sender-scoped tools in delegated runs

question: Should a senderless authenticated operator call to a valid persisted child session, and the private matching subagent-completion continuation, be treated as a trusted resumption of the original requester’s spawn-time sender-policy snapshot?
rationale: This is an intentional authorization and upgrade-policy choice: source can verify the predicates, but it cannot establish whether persistent delegated authority should survive later sender-policy edits or operator-driven resumption.

options.title: Approve bounded trusted resumption
options.body: Accept the documented snapshot model when persisted child lineage or the private matching completion handoff proves the continuation is internal.

options.title: Require fresh sender-policy resolution
options.body: Reject snapshot inheritance for senderless resumes and redesign the flow around a newly authenticated external requester or an explicit operator policy.

recommendation.title: Approve bounded trusted resumption
recommendation.body: Accept the documented snapshot model when persisted child lineage or the private matching completion handoff proves the continuation is internal.

likelyOwner.reason: The current proposal and its explicit authorization model are concentrated in this PR’s commits; a repository owner should make the final policy call with this contributor’s implementation context.
